title: Linkability of registration data
description: Parent's registration data (email, government ID) can be linked with other datasets to create a profile.
assumptions: Data is stored in a way that allows cross-referencing with external datasets.

title: Direct identification of parent
description: Authentication service can uniquely identify the parent using provided identifiers (name, government ID).
assumptions: Service retains identifiers for user authentication.

title: Lack of non-repudiation for registration
description: Parent could deny registration if logs are not tamper-proof or accessible.
assumptions: Registration actions are logged but logs may lack integrity controls.

title: Unauthorized access during transmission
description: Sensitive data (password, government ID) intercepted if flow is not encrypted.
assumptions: Transmission security (e.g., TLS) is not enforced.

title: Insecure storage of sensitive data
description: Government ID and password stored without adequate encryption or access controls.
assumptions: Data is persisted in the authentication service.

title: Lack of transparency in data usage
description: Parent not informed about how registration data will be used or shared.
assumptions: Privacy policy is not presented during registration.

title: Non-compliance with data protection laws
description: Handling government ID without legal basis or consent mechanisms.
assumptions: Service does not adhere to GDPR/CCPA requirements for sensitive data.

title: Data Disclosure to Data Store
description: Parent account personal data is being disclosed to and stored in the MongoDB data store. This represents an explicit data disclosure that should follow the minimality principle - only storing data strictly required for authentication purposes.
assumptions: Parent account data contains personal information subject to privacy protection

title: Identifiability of Parent Account Data
description: The MongoDB users collection stores parent account information that could directly identify individuals. If this data is accessed without proper authorization, individuals could be identified.
assumptions: Parent account data contains direct identifiers such as usernames, emails, or account IDs

title: Linkability Across Data Store
description: Parent account data stored in MongoDB could be linked with other data in the same or related collections to create comprehensive user profiles, potentially revealing more information than intended.
assumptions: Multiple data collections exist that could be correlated with parent account data

title: User Unawareness of Data Storage
description: Users may not be fully aware that their parent account data is being stored in the MongoDB data store, or may not understand the scope and purpose of this storage.
assumptions: Privacy notices may not clearly communicate data storage practices

title: Regulatory Compliance Risk
description: Storage of parent account personal data in MongoDB must comply with data protection regulations (e.g., GDPR, CCPA). Improper storage practices could lead to non-compliance.
assumptions: Parent account data is subject to data protection regulations

title: Unauthorized interception of JWT and user data in transit
description: JWT tokens and user data transmitted from Authentication Service to Parent User could be intercepted by unauthorized parties if the data flow is not properly encrypted or secured.
assumptions: Data flow uses standard transport security; no additional encryption beyond TLS assumed

title: Parent user identifiable from data in transit
description: JWT tokens and associated user data in the flow could be used to identify the parent user if intercepted, as JWTs typically contain user identifiers and claims.
assumptions: JWT contains user-identifying information as per standard implementation

title: Linkability of parent to authentication events
description: The data flow could be used to link the parent user to specific authentication events or child account activities, creating a privacy concern through correlation.
assumptions: Multiple authentication flows could be correlated over time

title: Parent unaware of data processing implications
description: Parent user may not be fully aware of what user data they are receiving, how it should be handled, or the privacy implications of storing JWT tokens.
assumptions: Parent users may lack technical understanding of JWT and data handling requirements

title: Linking child account to parent email
description: Authentication service links child's account to parent's email, enabling tracking across sessions and potential profiling.

title: Identifying child via parent email
description: Parent email used as identifier for child, exposing child's identity to the authentication service.

title: Data interception during login
description: Parent email and password transmitted without encryption, risking interception by attackers.

title: Insecure storage of credentials
description: Authentication service stores parent email and password insecurely, leading to potential data breach.

title: Child unaware of data processing
description: Child may not be informed about how their login data is processed and stored, violating transparency principles.

title: Non-compliance with child privacy regulations
description: Authentication service may not comply with COPPA or similar regulations regarding child data handling and parental consent.

title: Unauthorized disclosure of child profile data
description: The Authentication Service (P1) sends child profile information along with JWT to the child user. If the service does not properly validate the recipient or encrypt the data, sensitive child information could be disclosed to unauthorized parties.
assumptions: Child profile data contains personally identifiable information that requires protection

title: Linkability of child activities through JWT
description: The JWT containing userType 'child' and child profiles transmitted over this flow could be intercepted and used to link different activities of the same child user across the system, creating a comprehensive activity profile.
assumptions: JWT is transmitted without end-to-end encryption or could be logged by intermediate systems

title: Identifiability of child user in transit
description: Child profile data and JWT in transit could be intercepted, allowing identification of the specific child user. This is particularly sensitive given the child's age and privacy protections.
assumptions: Data flow is not fully encrypted or could be subject to man-in-the-middle attacks

title: Child unaware of data being shared
description: The child user (EE2) may not be aware of what profile data is being shared with them or how it will be used, especially given their age and potential lack of understanding of privacy implications.
assumptions: Child users may not have capacity to understand data sharing implications

title: Non-compliance with child privacy regulations
description: Receiving and processing child profile data may not comply with child-specific privacy regulations (e.g., COPPA, GDPR-K) if proper consent mechanisms and data handling procedures are not in place.
assumptions: Child data requires special regulatory protections that may not be fully implemented
uncertainty_note: Specific regulatory requirements depend on jurisdiction

title: Excessive Child Data Collection
description: Process P3 may collect and store more personal data in child profiles than strictly necessary for the intended purpose, violating data minimality principles.
assumptions: Child profile fields include non-essential personal data (e.g., detailed behavioral logs, contact info beyond requirements).

title: Identifiable Child Data Storage
description: MongoDB collection DS2 stores child profile data in a directly identifiable format without anonymization or pseudonymization, enabling identification of children.
assumptions: Child profiles contain unique identifiers (e.g., names, IDs) without privacy-preserving transformations.

title: Cross-System Child Data Linkability
description: Stored child profiles in DS2 can be linked with other datasets (e.g., school records, health data) via shared identifiers, enabling profiling.
assumptions: Child profile data includes persistent identifiers (e.g., student IDs) that exist in external systems.

title: Unauthorized Access to Child Profiles
description: MongoDB data store DS2 may be vulnerable to unauthorized access (e.g., via weak access controls, breaches), exposing sensitive child data.
assumptions: DS2 lacks robust encryption, access logging, or role-based access controls for child profile data.

title: Non-Compliance with Child Data Regulations
description: Storage of child profiles in DS2 may violate legal requirements (e.g., COPPA, GDPR-K) regarding consent, data retention, or security for minors' data.
assumptions: DS2 does not implement age-appropriate consent mechanisms or data retention policies compliant with child privacy laws.

title: Linkability of child's activities to identity
description: Child's video search, like, and comment actions can be linked to their identity by the Video Management Service, enabling profiling.
assumptions: Service retains user activity logs tied to account identifiers.

title: Identifiability via metadata in transit
description: Metadata in the data flow (e.g., timestamps, device IDs) could be used to identify the child user during transmission.
assumptions: Flow includes identifiable metadata not stripped before transmission.

title: Lack of non-repudiation for child's actions
description: Child cannot deny having performed actions (e.g., likes, comments) as the service logs them without explicit consent mechanisms.
assumptions: Service does not provide opt-out for action logging.

title: Unauthorized disclosure of child's data
description: Video Management Service may share child's activity data with third parties without adequate safeguards.
assumptions: Service has data-sharing agreements with external partners.

title: Data integrity violation in transit
description: Child's comments or requests could be altered during transmission, leading to misrepresentation of their actions.
assumptions: Flow lacks end-to-end encryption or integrity checks.

title: Child unaware of data collection scope
description: Child user may not understand what data is collected during video interactions (search, likes, comments).
assumptions: Privacy notices are not child-friendly or prominently displayed.

title: Non-compliance with child privacy regulations
description: Video Management Service may fail to comply with laws like COPPA regarding data handling for child users.
assumptions: Service lacks age verification or parental consent mechanisms.

title: Identified information in video metadata
description: The MongoDB videos collection stores video metadata that may contain personally identifiable information such as user IDs, timestamps, device identifiers, or location data. This metadata can be used to identify individuals associated with the videos.
assumptions: Video metadata includes user-identifying fields as is common in video management systems

title: Implicit data disclosure through video storage
description: The Video Management Service stores video metadata and files that may contain personal data beyond what is strictly necessary. This represents an implicit disclosure of personal data that could be minimized through better data collection practices.
assumptions: Video metadata and files may contain personal data that exceeds minimality requirements

title: Linkability through video metadata
description: Video metadata in transit between the Video Management Service and MongoDB could enable linking of different data points to identify individuals, especially when combined with other system data.
assumptions: Video metadata contains fields that could be correlated with other data sources

title: Excessive child data storage
description: The MongoDB datastore stores child search and watch history, which may exceed the minimality principle. Storing detailed behavioral data about children creates unnecessary privacy exposure when less detailed or aggregated data might suffice.
assumptions: The system stores detailed search queries and watch history rather than aggregated or anonymized data

title: Linkability of child behavioral data
description: Child search and watch history stored in the datastore can be linked across time to build detailed profiles of individual children's interests, preferences, and behaviors, enabling re-identification and profiling.
assumptions: The datastore retains historical data that can be queried and linked to specific child profiles

title: Identifiability through behavioral patterns
description: Search and watch history can uniquely identify children through their behavioral patterns, especially when combined with other stored data, making anonymization difficult.
assumptions: The data contains sufficient detail to distinguish individual children through their search/watch patterns

title: Lack of awareness about data collection
description: Children and parents may not be aware that search and watch history is being stored, violating the principle of informed consent and transparency in data processing.
assumptions: The system does not provide clear notice about what behavioral data is being collected and stored

title: Potential regulatory non-compliance
description: Storing detailed child behavioral data may violate child privacy regulations such as COPPA, GDPR-K, or other jurisdiction-specific requirements for children's data protection.
assumptions: The system operates in jurisdictions with child data protection regulations
uncertainty_note: Regulatory requirements vary by jurisdiction; specific compliance assessment needed

title: Unauthorized access to video data during upload
description: Video data transmitted without encryption could be intercepted by attackers during upload.
assumptions: Assumes no end-to-end encryption is implemented for the upload flow.

title: Video data used beyond approval purpose
description: Video Management Service may use uploaded videos for analytics, marketing, or other purposes beyond the stated approval/rejection function without explicit consent.
assumptions: Assumes the service has secondary data processing capabilities not disclosed to users.

title: Non-compliance with data protection regulations
description: Improper handling of video data (e.g., retention, access controls) may violate GDPR, COPPA, or other privacy regulations.
assumptions: Assumes the service lacks adequate compliance measures for child-related data.

title: Video stream interception
description: The video stream transmitted to the child could be intercepted by unauthorized parties during transmission, exposing content that may be inappropriate or revealing the child's viewing habits.
assumptions: Video stream is transmitted over network without end-to-end encryption or with weak encryption

title: Child identification through flow metadata
description: Metadata in the video stream flow (timestamps, session IDs, device identifiers) could be used to identify which specific child is receiving content, enabling tracking of individual viewing patterns.
assumptions: Flow contains identifying metadata that could be correlated with child identity

title: Non-compliance with child privacy regulations
description: The Video Management Service may not comply with child privacy regulations (e.g., COPPA, GDPR-K) when streaming content to children, such as failing to obtain proper parental consent or implementing age-appropriate data minimization.
assumptions: Service may not have implemented all required child privacy safeguards
uncertainty_note: Context doesn't specify regulatory framework, but child data processing typically requires special compliance measures

title: Viewing history aggregation on child's device
description: The child's device could aggregate viewing history from multiple video streams, creating a detailed profile of the child's interests and behaviors that could be exploited.
assumptions: Child's device stores or processes viewing history data

title: Linking child to viewing patterns
description: The Video Management Service could link the child's identity to their specific video viewing patterns, enabling behavioral profiling and targeted content delivery.
assumptions: Service maintains records linking child identity to viewing activity

title: Explicit Data Disclosure to AI Engine
description: Child browsing data is explicitly disclosed to the AI Recommendation Engine, potentially exceeding minimality requirements if not strictly necessary for recommendations.
assumptions: AI engine processes more data than required for its function.

title: Identifiability via Child Browsing Data
description: Child browsing data may contain direct identifiers (e.g., user IDs, device fingerprints) enabling identification of the child.
assumptions: Data includes persistent identifiers not anonymized before transfer.

title: Linkability of Child Data Points
description: AI engine may link browsing data with other child profiles or external data sources, creating comprehensive behavioral profiles.
assumptions: AI engine correlates data across multiple sources.

title: Unawareness of Data Sharing
description: Children/parents may be unaware their browsing data is shared with the AI engine for recommendations.
assumptions: No explicit consent or transparency mechanisms in place.

title: Non-Compliance with Child Privacy Regulations
description: AI engine processing may violate regulations like COPPA if child data is used without parental consent or beyond permitted purposes.
assumptions: AI engine lacks compliance safeguards for child data.

title: Unintended Disclosure of Government ID Images
description: Government ID images stored in the file system may be disclosed to unauthorized parties if access controls or encryption at rest are insufficient.
assumptions: File system lacks proper access controls or encryption for sensitive data.
uncertainty_note: Assumes no explicit security measures are documented for DS4.

title: Non-Compliance with Data Protection Regulations
description: Storing government ID images may violate regulations (e.g., GDPR) requiring specific handling of sensitive personal data, such as encryption or retention limits.
assumptions: Storage practices do not align with applicable legal requirements for sensitive data.

description: JWT contains user identifiers, allowing identification of the user when accessed from localStorage.
